topic: Urgent Matter — Emergency / FSC / Concurrent Legal Pathway
user_query: Applicant appears to be in urgent distress or faces an imminent deadline. How do I respond?
variations: Applicant says they are in danger right now.
Applicant has a court date this week.
Applicant is about to be evicted/homeless.
Applicant says they have no food or money for their family.
part_a_general_info: Urgency in the PBSG context is BROADER than legal deadlines. It includes physical safety, basic needs, immigration status, child welfare, and mental health crises. Your response must be concurrent — emergency services + social services + legal pathway in parallel, NOT sequential. Urgency trigger list (any one qualifies): • Physical violence occurring or threatened (incl. family violence, workplace violence) • Self-harm or suicide risk (applicant or someone they are calling about) • Child abduction or imminent removal of a child • Immigration pass expiring within 14 days (or already expired) • Imminent homelessness, no food, no money for basic needs • Court date or legal deadline within 14 days • Applicant in police custody or detention (or their dependant is) • Medical emergency involving the applicant or a dependant Key numbers to have ready: • Police emergency: 999 • Ambulance / fire: 995 • National Mindline (24-hour national mental health hotline): 1771 • National Anti-Violence and Sexual Harassment Helpline (NAVH): 1800-777-0000 • SSO (Social Service Office for financial assistance) and FSC (Family Service Centre for social assistance) directories: https://www.msf.gov.sg/our-services/directories • PBSG Urgent Legal Consultation: same-day slots at the State Courts (see GEN3-I06)
triage_questions: Q1: Is there an immediate threat to the applicant's (or someone else's) life or physical safety right now?
Q2: Is the urgency about basic needs (food, shelter, money, child welfare, mental health support) rather than a specific legal step?
Q3: Is there a specific legal deadline within 14 days (court date, immigration deadline, filing deadline, injunction hearing)?
Q4: Does the applicant still have a legal matter that needs triaging after the urgent concern is addressed?

Q1.question: Is there an immediate threat to the applicant's (or someone else's) life or physical safety right now?

Q2.question: Is the urgency about basic needs (food, shelter, money, child welfare, mental health support) rather than a specific legal step?
Q2.if_not_sure: Route B as primary AND proceed to Q3 (concurrent)

Q3.question: Is there a specific legal deadline within 14 days (court date, immigration deadline, filing deadline, injunction hearing)?
Q3.if_yes: Route C (Urgent Legal Consultation — Same-Day State Courts Slot)
Q3.if_not_sure: Route C AND proceed to Q4 (concurrent)

Q4.question: Does the applicant still have a legal matter that needs triaging after the urgent concern is addressed?
Q4.if_yes: Route D (Return to GEN3-T01 for main triage)
Q4.if_no: Route E (Document urgency intake and close)
Q4.if_not_sure: Route D (Return to GEN3-T01 for main triage)

routing: Route A (Emergency Services — IMMEDIATE): Say to the applicant: "The most important thing right now is your safety. Please call 999 for police or 995 for ambulance." After the call, note the incident, escalate to PBSG Staff (Route F of GEN3-T01) and, if the applicant still has a legal matter, arrange a call-back to triage through GEN3-T06 starting from Q2.

Route B (SSO / FSC — PRIMARY): Direct the applicant to the nearest Social Service Office (SSO) and Family Service Centre (FSC). Say: "There are officers at Social Service Officers and social workers at Family Service Centres who may be able to help you. Let me help you find your nearest centre." Look up the SSO and FSC directory live: https://www.msf.gov.sg/our-services/directories — filter by the applicant's postal code. Provide the name, address, and phone number of the nearest SSO and FSC. If the applicant also has a legal issue, proceed concurrently to Route C or Route D as appropriate.

Route C (Return to GEN3-T01 and Escalate for Urgent Legal Consultation Assessment): Return to the main triage questions at GEN3-T01 to identify the appropriate scheme. If eligible for PBSG schemes, inform applicant, "Your matter sounds like it may be urgent. Let me check how best we can assist you. I will try to call you back by the end of today.” Take down: applicant name, contact, deadline date, brief matter, and answers to Q1-5 in GEN3-T01. Escalate to PBSG Staff immediately to check if applicant is eligible for Urgent Legal Consultation (same or next-day legal consultation). Refer intern to GEN3-I06 for full scheme details.

Route D (Return to GEN3-T01): Once the urgent concern is addressed (or pathway confirmed), return to the main triage questions at GEN3-T01 to identify the appropriate scheme for the underlying legal matter.

Route E (Document and Close): Record the urgent intake in the system with a clear note of the concern raised and the pathway given. Inform applicant that they may call back if a legal matter emerges later. Resources to share with the applicant: SupportGoWhere — social and financial assistance PBSG YouTube channel — webinars on common legal issues Singapore Legal Advice — directory of lawyers and legal advice over the phone for a small fee Law Society of Singapore — directory of lawyers Legal Services Regulatory Authority e-Services — search for lawyers by practice area Caveat (share with applicant): "These are third-party websites not affiliated with or endorsed by Pro Bono SG. We share them as general pointers only and cannot vouch for the service, fees, or outcomes. If you have any questions on these services, please reach out to them directly."

Route A.name: Emergency Services — IMMEDIATE
Route A.script: The most important thing right now is your safety. Please call 999 for police or 995 for ambulance immediately.
needs_to_know: Emergency services should be contacted before continuing legal triage when there is an immediate threat to life or physical safety.
prepare: Brief description of the immediate safety concern
intern_steps: Ask the applicant to contact emergency services immediately.
After the emergency call, note the incident and escalate to PBSG Staff.
If the applicant still has a legal matter, arrange a call-back to continue urgent triage from GEN3-T06 Q2.
caveats: Do not continue legal triage while immediate safety is at risk.

Route B.name: SSO / FSC — PRIMARY
Route B.script: There are officers at Social Service Offices and social workers at Family Service Centres who may be able to help you. Let me help you find your nearest centre.
needs_to_know: Use this route when the urgent issue is about basic needs such as food, shelter, money, child welfare, or mental health support.
prepare: Nearest SSO/FSC name, address, and phone number after lookup
intern_steps: Look up the SSO and FSC directory live using the applicant's postal code.
Provide the name, address, and phone number of the nearest SSO and FSC.
If the applicant also has a legal issue, continue concurrently to the appropriate legal route.
caveats: This social support pathway runs concurrently with legal triage where needed.

Route C.name: Return to GEN3-T01 and Escalate for Urgent Legal Consultation Assessment
Route C.script: Your matter sounds like it may be urgent. Let me check how best we can assist you. I will try to call you back by the end of today.
needs_to_know: PBSG Staff must assess whether the applicant is eligible for an urgent same-day or next-day legal consultation.
prepare: Answers to GEN3-T01 Q1-Q5 where applicable
intern_steps: Return to GEN3-T01 to identify the appropriate scheme if this is standalone urgent triage.
Escalate to PBSG Staff immediately for urgent legal consultation assessment.
Refer to GEN3-I06 for full urgent legal consultation scheme details.
caveats: Do not promise that the applicant qualifies for urgent legal consultation.

Route D.name: Return to GEN3-T01
Route D.script: Now that the urgent concern has been addressed or the urgent pathway has been confirmed, I will ask a few questions to identify the right legal help pathway.
needs_to_know: The underlying legal matter still needs normal first-contact triage.
prepare: Brief description of the underlying legal matter
intern_steps: Return to GEN3-T01 Q1 for main triage if this is standalone urgent triage.
If GEN3-T06 was nested under GEN3-T02 or GEN3-T03, resume the parent stream instead of restarting GEN3-T01.

Route E.name: Document and Close
Route E.script: I have noted the urgent concern and the pathway shared. You may call PBSG again if a legal matter emerges later.
needs_to_know: Use this route when there is no legal matter left to triage after the urgent concern is addressed.

guardrail: • Under s 33 of the Legal Profession Act 1966, only qualified, practising lawyers may give legal advice. You must NEVER: (a) interpret a legal document for the applicant; (b) apply the law to the applicant's facts; (c) predict the outcome of a case; (d) tell the applicant what they should do legally. • You MAY: (a) confirm scheme eligibility against objective criteria; (b) read out scheme descriptions verbatim; (c) explain PBSG hotline operations; (d) take down particulars and escalate to PBSG Staff. • If the applicant insists on legal advice, respond: “I’m an intern/volunteer and I’m not able to give legal advice. What I can do is help you find the right legal help avenue or direct you to a qualified lawyer.” • If in doubt at any point — escalate to PBSG Staff. • Protect applicant confidentiality. Do not discuss the applicant outside the hotline context. Do not retain personal data on personal devices and/or beyond the PBSG volunteering period.
